name: ParaSwap Augustus V6 arbitrary-call approval drain
summary: AugustusV6.uniswapV3SwapCallback() did not verify that msg.sender was a genuine Uniswap V3 pool and trusted the caller-supplied data for the payer and token, so anyone could invoke it directly and make the router transferFrom any wallet that had approved it.

loss.notes: ParaSwap reports approximately $24,000 lost in the initial malicious incident across four affected wallets and multiple EVM networks. Per-asset quantities are not published.

ageReset.description: The vulnerable callback executes in the diamond's own directly deployed runtime; later facet cuts did not select or replace that code.

sources.note: Reviewed the malicious exploit transaction and receipt, direct Augustus V6 callback call, creation transaction, core runtime at deployment and immediately before the exploit, all pre-exploit DiamondCut records, the official incident report, and the pinned white-hat reproduction. Transaction 0x4d341ef4ef5c86b74f0c373c030e2f807421d6dfa9b73932ef85f355267c9cbe directly invokes the vulnerable callback and transfers an approved victim's tokens through the attacker-selected route. The seed row's transaction 0x35a73969f582872c25c96c48d8bb31c23eab8a49c19282c67509b96186734e60 was sent by whitehat responder 0xfde0d1575ed8e06fbf36256bcdfa1f359281455a and is not used as the exploit anchor. The callback selector is served by Augustus V6's own runtime rather than a facet. That 22,508-byte runtime has hash 0x13fa9cc60a5a1f39501e40c8df5e725c304ef9af0b931a31935e3db50090bbdd at deployment and immediately before this exploit; the later facet cuts did not select or replace the vulnerable core code.

limitations: The official $24,000 loss is an approximate aggregate across four wallets and multiple EVM networks; per-asset quantities are not published.
